name: Social Affordance Reading and Mentalizing

mechanism_chain.description: Occupant entering a new social space performs a rapid affordance scan: detecting spatial features (seating, surfaces, circulation), inferring territorial claims, reading social orientations of current occupants. Scan duration: ~5-15 seconds for initial assessment.

data.finding: People entering new spaces perform rapid visual scans (3-15 seconds) to assess affordances and social configurations before committing to action
data.effect: Affordance scanning is rapid and automatic

data.finding: Eye-tracking shows systematic scanning patterns when entering social spaces, focusing on seating, territorial markers, and occupant orientations

justification.backing: Kirsh's work on epistemic action shows that affordance scanning is a fundamental cognitive strategy for reducing uncertainty before committing to action. The social affordance scan is a specific application: detecting where one can sit, who is approachable, what social mode is appropriate.
justification.qualifier: The 5-15 second estimate is derived from general affordance scanning; specific measurements in social architectural contexts are limited.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if social behavior is driven by explicit plans rather than rapid affordance reading; but evidence shows even deliberate actors scan affordances first.

mechanism_chain.description: Based on scan results, occupant forms a social action plan: where to sit, who to approach, what social mode to adopt. High affordance legibility → fast, confident plan. Low legibility → hesitation, anxiety, suboptimal placement.

data.finding: Affordance-based action planning reduces cognitive load compared to deliberative planning; well-structured environments enable faster, more confident action
Hesitation and anxiety increase when entering unfamiliar or ambiguous social spaces

justification.backing: The mechanism is Gibsonian: legible affordances enable direct perception-action coupling without deliberative planning. Social action plans (where to sit, who to approach) form automatically from affordance reading when the space is well-coded.
justification.qualifier: The legibility → confidence link is inferred from general affordance theory; direct measurement of social action plan formation in architectural contexts is limited.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if social behavior is determined by explicit social norms that override affordance reading; in highly ritualized settings (formal events), scripts may dominate affordances.

mechanism_chain.description: Good affordance reading → appropriate social behavior → positive social outcomes. Poor reading → territorial violation, awkward placement, social miscalibration.

data.finding: Social miscalibration (sitting too close, interrupting ongoing interactions, violating territorial markers) produces negative social outcomes and occupant discomfort
Well-designed social spaces (clear activity zones, legible seating arrangements) produce higher satisfaction and more appropriate social behavior

justification.backing: The outcome link is observational: spaces with clear social affordances produce fewer territorial violations and more appropriate social behavior. The mechanism (affordance reading → action calibration → outcomes) is the theoretical bridge.
justification.qualifier: The causal chain involves inference; confounds (population differences, management factors) may contribute to observed outcome differences.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if social outcomes are determined by individual social skills rather than environmental legibility; some individuals navigate ambiguous spaces well regardless of design.

sensorimotor_coupling.description: Spaces supporting 3-5 distinct social modes (solitary, dyadic, small-group, large-group, observation) provide best overall social functioning. Below 3: too constrained. Above 5: too complex to read quickly.

low.description: Can transition between social modes without leaving the space — movable furniture, adjacent zones, visual/acoustic gradients

high.description: Must leave the space entirely to change social mode — separate rooms, locked doors, floor changes

key_references: Gibson, J. J. (1979). The Ecological Approach to Visual Perception. Houghton Mifflin.

cross_template_interactions.IC2: Body Budget Prediction — affordance reading is a cognitive cost (scan time, mentalizing load). High legibility reduces this cost; low legibility increases it. In novel or ambiguous social environments, the affordance scan generates social prediction error that feeds IC2.
cross_template_interactions.AX4: Perceived Control — readable social affordances provide AX4 by giving the occupant confidence in their social action plan. Unreadable spaces produce social helplessness — the occupant cannot determine what social behavior is appropriate.
